2609.05806.title: Exposing Weaknesses in Emotion Recognition in Conversations
2609.05806.paper_summary: Emotion Recognition in Conversations (ERC) aims to identify speakers' emotions in multi-turn dialogue. Accurate emotion recognition can support a wide range of applications, including empathetic conversational agents, mental health support, and educational technologies. While many recent approaches rely on task-specific fine-tuning, such models may exploit dataset-specific cues. A central yet rarely questioned assumption in ERC is that each utterance can be assigned a single unambiguous emotion label. To investigate this assumption, we study ERC using Large Language Models (LLMs) in a zero-shot setting while incorporating preceding conversational turns as context. We show that aggregate metrics mask systematic failures. Errors concentrate around utterances containing negations, exclamations, and interjections. This pattern is consistent across all evaluated models, suggesting limitations in the benchmarks rather than model-specific weaknesses. A controlled re-annotation study involving four human annotators supports this finding: strong agreement is observed in only 35 percent of cases, with neutral utterances dominating high-agreement instances, while many emotional categories fall into low-agreement regimes. These findings suggest that many apparent model errors reflect genuine annotation ambiguity rather than poor emotion understanding. Standard single-label evaluation is therefore insufficient. To address this limitation, we introduce an LLM-as-Judge framework that evaluates each emotion independently according to its plausibility in the conversational context rather than enforcing a single-label decision.
2609.05806.paper_summary_zh: 情感識別在對話中（ERC）旨在識別多輪對話中講話者的情感。準確的情感識別可以支持廣泛的應用，包括富有同理心的對話代理、心理健康支持和教育技術。儘管許多最近的方法依賴於特定任務的微調，但這些模型可能會利用數據集特定的線索。在ERC中，一個中心但很少受到質疑的假設是，每個發言都可以被分配一個單一的明確情感標籤。為了調查這一假設，我們在零樣本設置中使用大型語言模型（LLMs）研究ERC，同時將之前的對話輪次納入上下文。我們顯示出總體指標掩蓋了系統性失敗。錯誤集中在包含否定詞、感嘆詞和插入語的發言周圍。這一模式在所有評估的模型中是一致的，這表明基準測試的局限性，而非模型特定的弱點。一項涉及四名人類標註者的控制再標註研究支持了這一發現：只有35%的案例中觀察到強一致性，中立發言主導了高一致性實例，而許多情感類別則落入低一致性範疇。這些發現表明，許多明顯的模型錯誤反映了真正的標註模糊性，而非情感理解不佳。因此，標準的單標籤評估是不足夠的。為了解決這一局限性，我們引入了一個LLM作為評判框架，根據情感在對話上下文中的合理性獨立評估每個情感，而不是強制執行單標籤決策。
